source.publication: Publication 120 Retirement Income (December 2025), with the 2025 IL-1040 Instructions and Form IL-1040
source.section: Pub 120 PDF page 2 'What retirement income may I subtract', PDF page 3 'What federally taxed income may I not subtract'; Form IL-1040 Line 5; Instructions PDF page 7, Line 5; Form IL-1040 PDF page 1, Lines 1-19; Instructions PDF page 8, Lines 10-12; rate Instructions PDF page 1; Line 10a chart and Income Exceptions, Instructions PDF page 8

worked: Federal AGI = wages (person 0) 32,850.00 + NY government pension (person 0) 48,000.00 = 80,850.00. Federal taxable income = 80,850.00 - standard deduction 15,750.00 = 65,100.00 (federal senior deduction ignored; federal figures are given, not tested; Illinois starts from federal AGI). Form IL-1040 Line 1 federal AGI 80,850.00. Line 2 federally tax-exempt interest 0.00. Line 3 other additions 0.00. Line 4 = 80,850.00. Line 5 NY government pension 48,000.00 = 48,000.00. Lines 6 and 7 0.00. Line 8 = 48,000.00. Line 9 base income = 80,850.00 - 48,000.00 = 32,850.00. Income Exceptions: federal AGI 80,850.00 is not greater than 250,000.00, so the allowance stands. Line 10a 2,850.00. Line 10b 0.00. Lines 10c and 10d 0.00. Line 10 = 2,850.00. Line 11 net income = 32,850.00 - 2,850.00 = 30,000.00. Line 12 tax = 30,000.00 x 4.95% = 1,485.0000. Lines 13-18 0.00 (no credits in the projection). Line 19 state income tax = 1,485.00. Pub 120 limits the subtraction to 'a government retirement' plan, with no limit to Illinois; no sentence names another state, so this rests on that wording (settlement note 1).
